newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 11.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The government will be asked this week to approve new projects providing up to 4,000 jobs, including one involving IBM, the U.S. computer multinational.
- A major security alert has arisen over an apparent attempt by the IRA to launch mortar or bomb attacks on security bases in border areas of Northern ireland.
- The writer Salman Rushdie wants the EU to end its contacts with the Iranian government unless there is some movement towards lifting the death threat made against him almost eight years ago.
- The SDLP leader John Hume is to meet the Sinn Fein president, Gerry Adams for discussions on Thursday.
- If the IRA resumes its ceasefire the Irish government could resume discussions with Sinn Fein immediately, the Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Tuesday.

- More than 70 million Irish pounds was wiped off the value of Kerry Group on the Irish stock market on Tuesday after the company's own brokers downgraded 1997 earnings forecasts for the agri-business group.
- A petrol price rise of 5p a gallon and increases in the top rate of stamp duty on houses are being considered to fund the abolition of service charges and residential property tax.
- The property market is continuing to boom - particulary in Dublin where prices for new homes jumped 18p in the last year.
- The talks about the public sector element of the new national pay deal were adjourned on Tuesday night without agreement.
- Compensation for sectarian arson attacks during the summer cost the British taxpayer 17 million pounds, the equivalent of seven new primary schools, North Secretary Patrick Mayhew said on Tuesday.
- There is at best, only a 20 percent chance that the EMU will go ahead on schedule in early 1999, a leading international bank economist warned on Tuesday.
